sources.title: Anton O. Zakharov: State Formation in First Millennium Southeast Asia: A Reappraisal (2019)
sources.note: Original article directly read, introduction, royal epigraphy, territorial division and conclusions. Preserves disagreement about state formation instead of adopting either a unitary empire or an absence of states as settled. Chinese accounts distinguished from local inscriptions.

sources.title: UNESCO: Temple Zone of Sambor Prei Kuk, Archaeological Site of Ancient Ishanapura
sources.note: Official listing directly indexed/read: architectural materials, flying palaces, hydraulic features and continued modifications. Conflicting counts of octagonal shrines within the page are not repeated; broad empire wording is qualified with historical scholarship.

sources.title: Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art: Sambor Prei Kuk
sources.note: Original museum page directly read: seventh-to-ninth-century complexes, brick/sandstone/laterite, octagonal forms and regional artistic connections. No exclusive invention claim.

sources.title: DHARMA: K. 604, South Doorjamb of temple S at Sambor Prei Kuk, 549 Saka
sources.note: Original critical digital edition and Dominic Goodall 2019 translation directly read, stanzas 7-15. Date 549 Saka corresponds to 627 CE. Governor, learned official, friends and village endowment; modern translation distinguishes praise from evidence.

sources.title: DHARMA: K. 127, Doorjamb from Trapeang Prey, 604 Saka
sources.note: Kunthea Chhom critical edition directly read; Old Khmer, seventh-century lettering, line 4 new reading 604 versus Coedes 605. French translation retains old date but supports food and family lists. English gloss of the short date fragment uses the revised numeral. No modern Khmer glyph substitution or world-first claim.

sources.title: Shimoda Ichita, Chan Vitharong and Chhum Menghong: Large Terrace Structure Unearthed in the Heart of Isanapura (2025)
sources.note: Original published excavation article directly read, abstract, sections 4.1-4.3 and 6; M.90 terrace, artifacts and mid-sixth-to-mid-seventh-century construction range. Great Hall identification remains a hypothesis. Artifact fragments/counts are not equated with numbers of complete pots or households.

sources.title: Ichita Shimoda, Etsuo Uchida and Kojiro Tsuda: Estimated Construction Order of Sambor Prei Kuk Shrines (2019)
sources.note: Original article directly read, abstract, sections 1-4 and conclusions. Analyzed 59 brick structures; composition/thickness reveals multiple construction stages. Later additions explicitly distinguished from seventh-century fabric.

sources.title: University of Tsukuba Shimoda Laboratory: Digital Archive of Sambor Prei Kuk
sources.note: Research-team archive directly read, purpose and methodology. Local residents, field surveys, LiDAR terrain and surviving brick mounds. Public narrative avoids volatile exact archive counts.

proposedOverrides.name: Chenla and early Khmer centers
proposedOverrides.summary: Early Khmer royal and temple centers, with debated political unity and a transition into the Angkorian period.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Exact indexed record only; no chenla or zhenla indexed aliases found. Existing khmer-empire remains a separate later narrative.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Identical polygons in world-600 and world-700 cover approximately 103.927639 to 107.635676 E and 11.843115 to 16.188233 N. World-800 expands west and south, approximately 102.181622 to 107.898479 E and 8.475407 to 14.913592 N. These are schematic atlas snapshots, not verified annual boundaries.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: 600 is a map start, not a securely established founding year. Seventh-century Ishanapura evidence is distinct from disputed regional configurations and the ninth-century Angkorian transition. No forced 900 conquest event or successor link.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: UNESCO uses empire language, but specialist scholarship debates unity and territorial structures. Public prose preserves this. K.127 is a separate regional Old Khmer witness from Trapeang Prey, not a Sambor Prei Kuk inscription. Its modern reading 604 differs from older 605. No general medicine/toilet practice asserted without evidence.
